omissions: Assumption: the owner installs reviewed artifacts under immutable versioned root-owned paths; those paths are not reassigned while a job can use them.
Assumption: backend root, the host kernel and the pinned VMM are trusted infrastructure; guest code has no host mount, network device or forwarded credential.
Each backend job ID has an exclusive retained intent; unknown effects are not cleared and reused automatically. Actual filesystem durability is not established by the finite model.
The native client reloads its authoritative claim and authorization before launch and acceptance; a remote guest can finish privately after a delayed disconnect but cannot advance a cancelled claim.
Guest PID1 and monitor privilege separation, distinct check UID and absence of inherited serial descriptors need actual image/runtime verification.
Both sampled containment watchers must become ready and remain live; read-only filesystems and privilege separation are independent boundaries, not consequences of a marker.
No live KVM boot or owner-installed subsystem has been observed in this implementation session.
Base rootfs source-build provenance, runtime dependency closure and artifact reproducibility need real supplied inputs and independent review.
Finite TLA models do not establish Linux isolation, wall-time behavior or complete syscall detection.
Trusted-administrator mutation of versioned artifact paths during a job is outside the model and forbidden by the installation procedure.
Protocol action-map and fault-window renderers are unavailable; implementation correspondence remains an explicit review task.
A Git archive does not provide original Git history; checks requiring it are unsupported rather than given a fabricated HEAD.
